question: Which regulations put the heaviest ongoing burden on a 40-person fintech, and what kind of work drives it?

program.title: Compliance burden profile for a 40-person fintech
program.thesis: Judge each section's applicability to a specific company profile, then classify the work each applicable section creates and how heavy and recurring it is. Rolling up by regulation and work type shows where the burden actually comes from.

unit.rationale: Sections are the right grain for 'what does this rule make me do'.

nodes.label: Applies?
nodes.question: Would this section impose requirements on a 40-person US fintech that offers consumer payment accounts through a mobile app, markets online and by email, and stores customers' financial data?
nodes.why: Applicability gate for this company profile.

nodes.label: Work type
nodes.question: What is the main kind of work this section creates for the company?

options.description: Security or technical controls to build, buy, or configure
Designated responsible people, staffing, or training
Ongoing monitoring, testing, audits, or risk assessments
Disclosures, notices, or consents shown to customers
Reports or filings to regulators or the board

nodes.label: Effort
nodes.question: For a 40-person company, how much effort does complying with this section take?
levels: Heavy: a program needing dedicated staff or tooling

nodes.label: Recurring?
nodes.question: Does complying with this section require recurring work (periodic tests, reviews, reports, training, or renewals) rather than a one-time setup?
